```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "src")
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from api_client import USGSClient
from data_processor import process_quakes, summary_stats
from visualizations import recent_table, strongest_table, significant_table

_c = USGSClient()
df = process_quakes(_c.get_feed("all_day"))
sig = process_quakes(_c.get_feed("significant_week"))
stats = summary_stats(df, sig)
updated = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")

# Map/catalog records: real earthquakes with coords and non-negative magnitude.
_map = df[(df["type"] == "earthquake") & df["lat"].notna() & df["mag"].notna() & (df["mag"] >= 0)]
quake_records = _map[["lon", "lat", "mag", "place", "depth", "time_str"]].replace({np.nan: None}).to_dict("records")
ojs_define(quakes=quake_records)
```

```{ojs}
  projection: "equal-earth",

  color: {
    type: "linear", scheme: "YlOrRd", reverse: true,
    domain: [0, 300], label: "Depth (km)", legend: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.sphere({ fill: "#eef1f6", stroke: "#cbd3df" }),
    Plot.geo(land, { fill: "#e3ddcf", stroke: "#cdbfa5" }),
    Plot.dot(quakes, {
      x: "lon", y: "lat", r: "mag", fill: "depth",
      stroke: "#fff", strokeWidth: 0.4, strokeOpacity: 0.5, fillOpacity: 0.68,
      sort: "mag",  // draw stronger quakes on top so they aren't buried in clusters
      title: d => `M${d.mag} · ${d.place}\n${d.depth} km deep · ${d.time_str} UTC`,
      tip: true
    })
  ]
})
```

# About

::: {.card title="How this dashboard works — automated, open-source data delivery"}

**Quake Radar** is a live, **open-source** demo of *automated data delivery*: raw public data
in, a polished self-updating dashboard out — with **zero server and zero cost**.

**The pipeline (fully open, auditable):**

```
USGS GeoJSON API  →  Python (pandas + great-tables)  →  Quarto dashboard  →  GitHub Pages
        \____________ refreshed every 30 min by GitHub Actions (cron) ____________/
```

- **No server, no cost, no API key.** The USGS feeds are public; a GitHub Actions cron re-fetches,
  re-renders and redeploys every 30 minutes.
- **Verifiable by design.** Every number traces back to the public source cited in the
  *Source* footer on each page (USGS, with a link to its documentation) and to the open code.
- **Open methodology.** The code that fetches and transforms the data is on GitHub; fork it,
  read it, reuse it.

**Built & maintained by Ronald Mego** — data & analytics.
Code: [github.com/ronaldmego/quake-radar](https://github.com/ronaldmego/quake-radar) ·
Profile: [github.com/ronaldmego](https://github.com/ronaldmego)

**Data & responsibility.** Source: [USGS Earthquake Hazards Program](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/)
(public domain). This is an informational dashboard, not an official alert system — for emergencies and
official guidance always refer to your national agency (e.g. **FUNVISIS** in Venezuela) and the
official USGS event pages linked in each table.

:::
